original_question: Let A be a set of nonnegative integers containing 0 such that each iterated sumset hA has asymptotic density 0, even though A subset 2A subset 3A subset ... is an increasing chain. Must any nontrivial structure nevertheless appear in this sequence of sumsets, and if so, what must happen?
target_in_paper: The draft most closely targets the open-ended iterated-sumsets problem in Section 2010.1.2 ("Schnirelman") of the CANT problem sessions: let 0 ∈ A, assume d_L(hA) = 0 for every h ≥ 1, and ask whether any structure must nevertheless appear in the increasing chain A ⊆ 2A ⊆ 3A ⊆ ···. This is the nearest official formulation in the paper, and it is clearly a different section from any numbered Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures almost all of the mathematical core that appears in the paper: the ambient set is the nonnegative integers, 0 is assumed to lie in A, the objects of interest are the iterated sumsets hA, each hA is required to have asymptotic density 0, the family A ⊆ 2A ⊆ 3A ⊆ ··· is the relevant chain, and the paper's actual question is exactly whether some unavoidable structure must still emerge in that zero-density situation. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))
missing_details: The paper uses the notation d_L(B) for asymptotic density in this passage, defined by d_L(B) = lim_{n→∞} B(n)/n when the limit exists, where B(n) counts elements of B up to n. Your draft should make that definition explicit rather than just saying "asymptotic density". ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))

The quantifier is "for all h ≥ 1"; the problem is about every iterated sumset hA, not just infinitely many h or some sufficiently large h. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))

The notation hA should be defined self-containedly as the h-fold sumset A + ··· + A. The paper assumes additive-combinatorics notation, but a stand-alone question should spell it out. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))

The ambient semigroup should be stated explicitly as N_0 = {0,1,2,...} (the nonnegative integers), since the paper phrases the problem for sets of non-negative integers containing 0. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))

The inclusion chain A ⊆ 2A ⊆ 3A ⊆ ··· is mathematically redundant once 0 ∈ A is assumed; it is part of the paper's wording, but in a sharpened stand-alone question it should be presented as a consequence of 0 ∈ A rather than as an independent hypothesis. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should preserve the contrast stated immediately beforehand: if d_L(hA) > 0 for some h and d = gcd(A), then some h_0A eventually coincides with d·N_0; the zero-density problem is asking what, if anything, must replace that kind of eventual periodic structure. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))

The nearby context also defines eventual coincidence X ∼ Y to mean that there exists N such that for all n ≥ N, n ∈ X iff n ∈ Y. That notion helps explain the intended contrast and should be included in the supporting context, even if not built into the final question itself. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))

The paper's formulation is intentionally open-ended: it does not ask for classification under extra assumptions, nor for a theorem about bounded gaps, eventual periodicity, arithmetic progressions, or any other specific structure. A faithful rewrite should keep that scope narrow and not over-specify the type of structure sought. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))
refined_question: Let A ⊆ N_0 := {0,1,2,...} with 0 ∈ A, and for each integer h ≥ 1 write hA := A + ··· + A (h summands). Assume that, for every h ≥ 1, the asymptotic density d_L(hA) exists and satisfies d_L(hA) = lim_{n→∞} |hA ∩ [1,n]|/n = 0. Since 0 ∈ A, the iterated sumsets form a nested chain A ⊆ 2A ⊆ 3A ⊆ ··· . Must some nontrivial additive structure nevertheless appear in the family {hA}_{h≥1}? Equivalently, is there any structural phenomenon that must occur for this increasing sequence of iterated sumsets despite the fact that every hA has asymptotic density 0? ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))
justification: The draft matches the 2010.1.2 Schnirelman problem almost verbatim: the source passage explicitly assumes 0 ∈ A, requires d_L(hA) = 0 for all h ≥ 1, writes the chain A ⊆ 2A ⊆ 3A ⊆ ···, and then asks whether, as one adds A to itself more and more times, "any structure" appears and whether there is "anything that must happen." The surrounding lines also provide the hidden context your draft leaves implicit: d_L is defined in this section, eventual coincidence X ∼ Y is defined, and the question is motivated by the preceding positive-density statement that if d_L(hA) > 0 for some h, then one eventually gets a structured set of multiples of gcd(A). That is why the sharpest faithful rewrite is still an open-ended structural question, rather than a more specific conjecture about periodicity, gaps, or arithmetic progressions. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))
